newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt sticks to U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt sticks to U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging market debt remained in lock step with U.S. Treasuries Friday as investors remained on the sidelines and Wall Street dealers lost incentive to make dramatic moves, traders said.
"The U.S. bond market gave us most of our direction," one Brady bond trader said. "On its own the Brady market did not do much."

The spreads of most major Latin American Bradies widened five to 10 basis points against U.S. Treasuries in thin activitity to end the week. Dealers saw this as unwinding of the market's recent rally to historically tight levels.
In the major Latin assets, Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR slipped 1/8 to 94-3/4, while Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR bonds lost 3/8 to 83-1/8.
The relatively high cost of emerging market assets seemed unlikely to derail the heady flow of funds into the market, as money managers seek assets that provide higher returns.

"For the new investor in the market these spreads look relatively cheap," said Gary Evans, emerging market debt strategist at UBS Securities. "As long as the U.S. equity market hangs in here, you're going to see this market trade in a range."
The only major news Friday came from the Philippines, where the central bank widened the peso's target range, but the country's Brady bonds paced the overall market.
Philippine FLBS-A widened five basis points to 93-7/8 and Pars lost around 14 basis points to 88-3/8, traders said.
